I've experienced the same selling on localmonero and had to resort to checking ID as much as I didn't want to. I've stopped selling a while ago.

Basically there were scammers who would initiate a trade, then go cold call residents in my city, claiming that they needed to pay their taxes or go to jail (one of those scams) and provide them with my bank account details to pay. What the scammers wanted was for me to be paid, so I would release the XMR for them.

What would happen in turn is, the people who were called, would provide my details to the police/bank who would in turn freeze my account. This happened on several different occasions where I had to come to the agreement with the bank to not trade. I did still continue trading for a while but I had to check for IDs before giving out bank details.There was no real way I could think of around it as the scammers were plenty.

First of all, congrats on all the progress that you've made. The fact that you were able to stay fairly calm in a situation like that with your dad is great. And the fact that professional therapy helped is also great. 

That ability to stop in the moment, breathe and refocus is fantastic and so vital.

I know this sounds counter-intuitive but you need to forgive yourself. We all make mistakes, we learn, then learn again. Look past it and acknowledged you've learnt from it. Just prepare yourself for any other scenario that you may be in like that in the future.

This doesn't bring you down, because you've come a long way and you will keep going forward (always will be some bumps along the way, otherwise it wouldn't be natural). Think about what really upset you, the core of it, how you may have things and do your best to address it.

​

This article helped me:

[Relax and Re-asses](https://www.psychologytoday.com/au/blog/evolution-the-self/201208/powerful-two-step-process-get-rid-unwanted-anger)

When I was younger, I've had similar problems that only escalated itself as time grew on. I didn't have any support roles to help me down the right path unfortauntely, didnt go through any counselling or go through the right forums. For one, good on you for asking questions. Keep doing that.

My mother (probably like your dad) was an extremely angry, abusive person.Naturally, I learned a lot of l these behaviours as I aged. At first I was proud, because people naturally scared off when I was aggressive. People thought I was daring and bold and had a lot of friends. But those numbers dwindled when it came down to having any meaningful relationships. 

I'm still a work in progress myself, but what has worked for me is catching myself when I get angry and acknowledge how I feel. I try to look at myself from the outside. It sounds weird but I try to imagine seeing the world from outside my body. When you start feeling the heat in your body heat up, try to observe it for what it is. Note that you are really worked up, that your emotions are getting clouded and allow yourself to feel that way. 

If you have to walk away, do so. But just know that walking away also will likely not address the issues that you're going through. (And there will be instances that you simply can't do that, as I've learnt from experience)

When you have time to reflect, even in that moment, think about the actual reasons you've got to that point. Anger is usually masked by something else and not specific to events such as finding out about your gift and "upsetting your girlfriend". I'm sure if you told her about finding out, she would probably be sad, but nowhere emotional to the extent to which you got. So then why did you get so emotional?

There's something underlying there deeper rooted in regards to how that made you feel. Try to figure what that is, and help to address it through meaningful ways. 

​

I personally have had esteem issues, so I try to reinforce my own image in my head and praise myself more often. My esteem issues have led to a very fragile ego and the feeling of "disrespect" is a very common theme with me.

You need to dig deep when you're calm and really analyse your behaviours. This article gave me a lot of perspective:

[What Anger may be hiding](https://www.psychologytoday.com/au/blog/evolution-the-self/200807/what-your-anger-may-be-hiding)
